title: Step Supporting Error Handling Unit Association Contract

scope.purpose: Define the Step-owned relationship that makes an Error Handling Unit instance applicable to a Step-defined target scope, including identity, multiplicity, invocation binding, change, dissociation, and historical provenance.
scope.appliesTo: A concrete Step specialization that associates one or more Error Handling Unit instances with Step, SPU, or other internal target scopes.

definition.association: An explicit Step Composition-owned relationship between one Error Handling Unit runtime instance and one target scope within one Step instance.
associationIsNot: Ownership of the Unit instance by the target.
Transfer of association-management, invocation, or lifecycle authority to the target.
An invocation, operation execution, operation target, or ErrorHandlerResult.
A guarantee that the Unit is currently admitted, ready, or executing.
A guarantee that every error occurrence in the target scope is eligible for handling.

identities.errorHandlingUnitIdentity: Identifies one concrete Error Handling Unit runtime instance independently of its associations.
identities.associationTargetIdentity: Identifies the target scope to which the Unit is applicable.
identities.errorHandlingUnitAssociationIdentity: Identifies one particular relationship between one Unit instance and one target scope within one Step instance.

permittedKinds: A specific SPU instance or SPU-defined internal scope.
The owning Step instance as a whole.
Another explicitly identified Step-internal scope, operation boundary, component, or context defined by the concrete Step.
rules: The common contract does not restrict an association target to an SPU.
The target scope is identified independently of the Unit instance and Association.
The target exposes or defines the context within which the Unit may be applicable; it does not transfer ownership or flow-control authority.
The concrete Step defines target identity representation, compatibility, and the precise scope of applicability.
associationTargetIdentity must distinguish the target scope kind and the concrete target instance within the owning Step.

permitted: One Unit instance may have multiple associations to distinct target scopes where the Step permits it.
Multiple Unit instances may be associated with the same target scope where the Step permits it.
notMandated: Exclusive use of a Unit by one target.
A universal maximum number of associations.
A universal requirement that every target have an associated Unit.
multiplicity.identityRule: Every association has its own identity even when the Unit instance or target scope is shared.

authorityAndOwnership.authority: The owning Step Composition is the sole authority for establishing, activating where applicable, changing, rebinding, deactivating, and ending Unit Associations.
rules: The Unit may consume the association context supplied for an invocation but may not create, select, mutate, replace, or terminate its own associations.
An SPU may be a target but does not thereby acquire authority over the Unit or its association.
Association does not transfer ownership of target resources, error occurrences, occurrence registries, Publisher instances, or operation results.
Step Composition retains association authority even when the technical implementation uses callbacks, references, registrations, or handles owned by another component.
separation: Association existence is distinct from Unit admission/readiness under the Lifecycle Contract.
Association existence is distinct from invocation authorization and operation execution.
Association termination is distinct from Unit instance release.
Association metadata retention is distinct from operation-result retention.

preconditions: The Unit instance is known to Step Composition and has a stable errorHandlingUnitIdentity.
The target scope is known and has an associationTargetIdentity within the owning Step instance.
The Unit satisfies the lifecycle and admission preconditions required by the concrete Step.
The Unit capability is compatible with the target scope under the Step specialization.
rules: Step Composition creates a distinct errorHandlingUnitAssociationIdentity for the relationship.
The association records the Step, Unit, and target identities as one explicit binding.
The association becomes eligible to authorize invocations only when the Step-defined establishment and activation conditions are satisfied.
Association establishment does not necessarily trigger an invocation or operation.

invocationBinding.rule: Every invocation performed under an association is bound to exactly one errorHandlingUnitAssociationIdentity and its corresponding associationTargetIdentity.
constraints: When a Unit instance has multiple associations, Step Composition explicitly selects the association for each invocation.
The association target identity supplied for an invocation must match the target bound to that association.
The Unit must not infer, substitute, or silently broaden the selected association scope.
An invocation already authorized under an association remains attributable to that original association if the association changes or ends while the invocation is in progress.
An operation may target specific Error Occurrences or other resources that are narrower than, or otherwise distinct from, the association target; this does not mutate the association binding.

rules: A change in applicability or target scope is an explicit Step Composition decision.
If the identity of the relationship changes, the preferred representation is to end the old association and establish a new association identity.
An in-flight invocation remains attributed to the association under which it was authorized.
The concrete Step defines how target access capabilities, registrations, and handles are updated and reconciled.
noImplicitEffects: Changing an association does not create, release, or replace the Unit instance.
Changing an association does not rewrite existing invocation identities or operation entries.
Changing an association does not resolve or delete Error Occurrences.
Changing an association does not decide the retention or aggregation of already produced operation results.

dissociation.authority: Step Composition exclusively coordinates and authorizes association termination.
rules: Dissociation ends the association's authority to authorize new invocations.
Dissociation does not automatically release or shut down the Unit instance.
Dissociation does not revoke operations already completed or entries already accepted.
The concrete Step defines whether an in-flight invocation may finish under its original association, must be cancelled, or must be reconciled before dissociation is complete.
Pending operations and produced-but-unaccepted results must be reconciled under the behavioral and lifecycle custody requirements.
Historical operation entries retain the original association and target provenance after dissociation.
Dissociation does not invalidate operation entries produced under the association.
Historical association identity remains interpretable while any invocation record, operation entry, recovery record, or aggregate refers to it.
Retaining association metadata does not require retaining the Unit runtime instance, target object, borrowed view, callback, or handle.
Association identities must not be reused while historical evidence may still refer to them.

required: Define concrete Step, Unit, target, and Association identity representations and uniqueness scopes.
Define permitted target kinds and target-scope compatibility rules.
Define allowed multiplicity, sharing, and exclusivity constraints.
Define establishment, activation, deactivation, change, and dissociation mechanics.
Define target access capabilities and their ownership/lifetime.
Define in-flight invocation and operation behavior during association change or dissociation.
Define how association identity and target provenance are carried into operation entries and retained recovery evidence.
specializationRequirements.completionRule: A concrete association specialization is complete when target scope, identity, multiplicity, authority, activation, invocation binding, dissociation, in-flight work, and historical provenance are explicit.

explicitNonGoals: No universal one-to-one mapping, cardinality, or exclusivity.
No transfer of ownership or authority to the association target.
No automatic Unit construction, admission, invocation, release, or result aggregation caused by association changes.
No mandatory global association registry or central association manager.
No assumption that association target equals the target of every handling operation.

references.relationship: Invocation, operation target, operation result, and provenance requirements under an association.
Detailed operation-attempt and publication protocol, subject to the broader association scope defined by the Supporting Unit contracts.
Admission and lifecycle preconditions for association establishment and use.
Step Composition authority over internal component association and lifecycle coordination.
Framework-level association coordination invariants refined by this specialized Association Contract; specialized identity names and behavior remain authoritative.

frameworkCoordination.conformance: This contract specializes the shared Step Composition coordination invariants. Where the shared contract defines only conceptual identity roles or lifecycle distinctions, this document supplies the component-specific identity names, semantics, mechanics, and constraints.
frameworkCoordination.precedence: The common contract governs cross-cutting Step Composition coordination invariants. This specialized contract governs component-specific behavior and mechanics. Neither contract changes the component pattern?s distinct behavioral result semantics.

frameworkIdentityRoleMapping.targetIdentitySemantics: associationTargetIdentity identifies both the target scope kind and the concrete target instance within the owning Step; it must not be represented by a bare SPU identity when the target scope may instead be Step-wide or another Step-internal scope.
